title: A simple C*-algebra with a unique irreducible representation class

content.display_title: A simple C*-algebra with a unique irreducible representation class
content.one_sentence_role: Establishes the properties that make the fixed algebra $T$ a counterexample to Naimark's problem.
content.natural_language_statement: Let $A$ be the completed CAR algebra. Let $\pi:A\to B(\mathcal H)$ be the direct sum of one chosen GNS representation from each pure-state GNS equivalence class, and let $(L_i)_{i\in I}$ be the unitaries obtained from the fixed CAR homogeneity and shell construction. Put $T=C^*(\pi(A)\cup\{L_i:i\in I\})\subseteq B(\mathcal H)$, and write $\iota(a)=\pi(a)$ for the embedding into $T$. Let $\rho_0:T\to B(\mathcal H)$ be the inclusion representation. Then $T$ is a nonzero, norm-closed, infinite-dimensional unital C*-algebra, $\iota$ is injective and unital, and $\rho_0$ is faithful and nonzero irreducible. Every nonzero irreducible $*$-representation $\rho:T\to B(K)$ on a complex Hilbert space $K$ is unitarily equivalent to $\rho_0$, even if $\rho(1)=1$ is not assumed: there is a unitary $U:\mathcal H\to K$ with $$U\rho_0(t)=\rho(t)U\qquad(t\in T).$$ The algebra $T$ is simple: every norm-closed two-sided ideal is $\{0\}$ or $T$. Moreover, for no complex Hilbert space $K$ is there an injective $*$-representation $e:T\to B(K)$ with $e(T)=\mathcal K(K)$.
content.assumptions: The automorphisms and shell unitaries are obtained from CAR homogeneity and fixed once. No simplicity or uniqueness-of-representation assumption is supplied to the theorem. The Hilbert space $K$ in the representation and compact-operator assertions is arbitrary; separability and preservation of the identity by the given representation are not assumed.
content.conclusion: Thus $T$ has exactly one unitary-equivalence class of nonzero irreducible $*$-representations, but is not isomorphic to the full algebra of compact operators on any Hilbert space. The nonzero, norm-closed algebra $T$, its injective unital embedding $\iota$ and its faithful irreducible inclusion $\rho_0$ are the same throughout these assertions.
content.proof_summary: Apply the cited theorem for a fixed shell family to the family supplied by CAR homogeneity. The construction and the representation-classification theorem give the embedding and unitary equivalences; their cited consequences give simplicity and the exclusion of an algebra of compact operators.

proof_steps.text: Let $o$ denote the class of the distinguished pure state, let $f_n$ be the decreasing root projections, and write $p_n=f_n-f_{n+1}$ for their shells. At $o$ choose $\alpha_{o}=\mathrm{id}$ and $w_{o,n}=p_n$. In each other class, CAR homogeneity supplies one automorphism $\alpha_i$, and exact shell matching supplies all $w_{i,n}$ for that same $\alpha_i$. These choices are made once for the entire construction.

The shell construction supplies an injective unital embedding $\iota$ and an irreducible inclusion $\rho_0$. Since $\iota$ embeds the infinite-dimensional algebra $A$, the algebra $T$ is infinite dimensional. Its norm closure is part of its construction, and its nonzeroness follows from injectivity of $\iota$.

The representation-classification theorem for this fixed family gives unitary equivalence with $\rho_0$ for every unital nonzero irreducible representation. The cited unitality lemma gives $\rho(1)=I_K$ for every nonzero irreducible $*$-representation $\rho$ of $T$, so the same conclusion applies without initially assuming that $\rho$ preserves the identity.

The cited simplicity theorem applies because $\rho_0$ is faithful and all nonzero irreducible representations are unitarily equivalent to it. The cited compact-operator exclusion applies because $T$ is unital and infinite dimensional. The Lean theorem collects these proved properties for the same algebra.

content.lean_realization_notes: In the displayed inclusion representation, one also has $T\cap\mathcal K(\mathcal H)=\{0\}$. This follows from the stated properties: the intersection is a closed two-sided ideal of $T$; if it were nonzero, simplicity would give $T\subseteq\mathcal K(\mathcal H)$. Then $I_{\mathcal H}$ would be compact, so $\mathcal H$, and hence $T\subseteq B(\mathcal H)$, would be finite dimensional, a contradiction. This is a consequence of the theorem, not an extra field of its Lean statement.
